examples.en: The expedition team returned after a month.
The players are scheduled to return tomorrow morning.
The astronauts returned safely to Earth.
After the war ended, the soldiers returned to their hometowns.
I sorted my photos on the plane back.
I am waiting for my family to come back.

explain: 멀리 갔다가 임무나 일정을 마치고 돌아올 때 쓰는 격식 있는 표현이에요. 일상에서는 '돌아오다', '집에 가다'를 써요. '무사히 귀환하다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: A formal expression for coming back after a mission or trip far from home. In daily speech use '돌아오다' or '집에 가다'. A common use is '무사히 귀환하다' (return safely).

examples.en: The sweltering heat is raging this summer.

examples.ko: 독감이 기승을 부려서 결석한 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: The flu is rampant, so many students are absent.

examples.ko: 황사가 기승이라 마스크 없이는 못 나가요.
examples.en: The yellow dust is so bad that I can't go out without a mask.

examples.ko: 추위가 기승을 부릴 때는 두껍게 입으세요.
examples.en: When the cold is at its worst, dress warmly.

examples.ko: 보이스피싱이 다시 기승을 부린다고 하니 조심하세요.
examples.en: They say voice phishing is rampant again, so be careful.
The worst of the heat has eased off a bit.

explain: 거의 '기승을 부리다'라는 덩어리로 외우면 돼요. 더위, 추위, 독감, 범죄처럼 좋지 않은 것이 한창 심할 때 쓰고, 좋은 일에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 요즘 감기가 기승을 부려서 병원마다 사람이 많아요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 것이 한창 심하게 퍼질 때 써요. '기승' 혼자서는 거의 쓰지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something bad is spreading or raging at its peak. '기승' is hardly ever used alone.

explain_en: Learn it as the chunk '기승을 부리다'. It is used when something bad, such as heat, cold, flu or crime, is at its peak, and never for good things.

examples.en: The light flickered and then suddenly went out.
I can see the starlight twinkling in the distance.
My eyes are tired, so they keep blinking.
When the traffic light flickers, the signal is about to change.
The screen flickers, so my eyes hurt.
The candle flame wavered and then went out in the wind.

explain: 불빛이 켜졌다 꺼졌다 하거나 눈이 감겼다 떠지는 모습에 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '깜박거리다', '깜빡거리다'도 써요. 뭔가를 잊었을 때는 '깜박하다'를 써서 뜻이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes a light going on and off or eyes closing and opening. '깜박거리다' and '깜빡거리다' mean the same thing. Forgetting something is '깜박하다', which has a different meaning.

examples.ko: 아기가 침대 위에 꼿꼿이 서서 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is standing upright on the bed, laughing.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 연세가 많으신데도 허리를 꼿꼿이 펴고 걸으세요.
examples.en: Grandpa is old, yet he walks with his back held straight.
In an interview, sit with your back straight.

examples.ko: 선생님은 칠판 앞에 꼿꼿이 서서 우리를 바라보셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher stood upright in front of the board and looked at us.
The cat comes over with its tail held straight up.

examples.ko: 동생은 혼나는 중에도 고개를 꼿꼿이 들고 있었어요.
examples.en: Even while being scolded, my younger sibling held their head high.

explain: 허리나 몸이 굽지 않고 곧게 서 있는 모습이라 '곧게'보다 뻣뻣하고 힘 있는 느낌이에요. 형용사 '꼿꼿하다'는 '성격이 꼿꼿하다'처럼 굽히지 않는 태도를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It describes the back or body standing straight without bending, with a stiffer, firmer feel than '곧게'. The adjective '꼿꼿하다' is used for an unbending attitude, as in '성격이 꼿꼿하다'.

examples.ko: 지금 우리 회사의 당면 문제는 인력 부족이에요.
examples.en: The problem our company faces right now is a labor shortage.

examples.ko: 우리는 지금 큰 위기에 당면해 있어요.
examples.en: We are facing a big crisis right now.

examples.ko: 졸업을 앞두고 많은 학생이 취업 문제에 당면하게 돼요.
examples.en: As graduation nears, many students come face to face with the job problem.
Let's solve the pressing things one by one, starting with the one in front of us.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 물 부족이라는 어려움에 당면했어요.
examples.en: That country is facing the difficulty of water shortage.

examples.ko: 어려운 상황에 당면하면 침착하게 생각해야 해요.
examples.en: When you face a difficult situation, you have to think calmly.

explain: '~에 당면하다'처럼 어려운 일, 문제, 위기가 눈앞에 닥쳤을 때 써요. '직면하다'와 거의 비슷하게 쓰는데, 당면은 '당면 과제'처럼 지금 해결해야 할 일을 가리킬 때 특히 많이 나와요. 말보다는 글이나 뉴스 말투예요.
explain_en: It is used as '~에 당면하다' when a difficulty, problem or crisis is right in front of you. It is used much like '직면하다', but 당면 appears especially in phrases like '당면 과제' for things that must be solved now. It sounds more like writing or news than casual speech.

examples.ko: 밤길에 누군가 뚜벅거리며 따라오는 소리가 들렸어요.
examples.en: On the night road I heard someone following with heavy footsteps.

examples.ko: 아버지가 복도를 뚜벅거려서 금방 오신 걸 알았어요.
examples.en: Dad's footsteps in the hallway told me he had just arrived.

examples.ko: 구두 소리가 뚜벅거리면 선생님이 오신 거예요.
examples.en: When shoes go clomp, clomp, it means the teacher has come.
He walked out with steady steps without saying a word.
Every night there's a sound of stomping from the upstairs apartment.
I wore my new boots and stomped on purpose.

explain: 무겁고 또렷하게 걷는 소리나 모습이에요. '뚜벅뚜벅'은 한 걸음씩 걷는 모양이고, '-거리다'를 붙이면 그 소리가 되풀이되는 동사가 돼요.
explain_en: It describes the sound or look of walking with heavy, distinct steps. '뚜벅뚜벅' is the adverb for step-by-step walking, and adding '-거리다' makes a verb for that sound repeating.

examples.ko: 경비원이 문 앞에서 막아서는 바람에 못 들어갔어요.
examples.en: The guard stood in my way at the door, so I couldn't go in.

examples.ko: 소 떼가 길을 막아서서 차가 한참 움직이지 못했어요.
examples.en: A herd of cows stood in the road, and cars couldn't move for a long time.
A stranger suddenly stepped in front of me and blocked my way.
My mom tried to stand in the way of me leaving.
Nobody could stop him.

examples.ko: 누가 막아서도 저는 포기하지 않을 거예요.
examples.en: Even if someone stands in my way, I won't give up.

explain: '막다'는 구멍, 길, 일 등 널리 쓰지만, 막아서다는 사람이 몸으로 앞에 서서 못 가게 하는 장면에 써요. '가로막다'는 길이나 시야를 막는 것에도 쓰는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: '막다' is used broadly for holes, roads and matters, but 막아서다 is for a person physically standing in front to stop someone from going. '가로막다' differs in that it can also be used for things blocking a road or a view.

examples.en: The weekend market is teeming with people.
I was startled because bugs were swarming under the fridge.
The pond is swarming with tadpoles.
The beach will be packed with people.
It was school vacation, so the amusement park was teeming with kids.

examples.ko: 바글거리는 지하철 안에서 서 있기가 힘들었어요.
examples.en: It was hard to stand in the jam-packed subway.

explain: 사람이나 벌레, 작은 생물이 좁은 곳에 빽빽하게 모여 움직일 때 써요. '북적거리다'는 사람이 많아 활기차게 붐비는 느낌이고, '바글거리다'는 작은 것들이 가득 우글대는 느낌이에요. '바글바글'로도 많이 말하고, 찌개가 '바글바글 끓다'처럼 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when people, bugs or small creatures are packed and moving around in a tight space. '북적거리다' feels like a lively crowd, while '바글거리다' feels like lots of small things swarming. It is also said as '바글바글', and used for stew bubbling, as in '바글바글 끓다'.

examples.en: If dry grass catches fire, it spreads fast.
The matches are wet, so they don't light well.
The curtain caught fire and everyone was shocked.
The burning firewood crackles.
The competition between the two companies has heated up.
Ever since the debate got heated, the meeting has run long.

explain: '불이 붙다'가 더 흔하게 쓰이고, '불붙다'는 한 단어로 붙여 써요. 남이 불을 옮길 때는 '불을 붙이다'이고 '불붙다'는 저절로 붙는 쪽이에요. 경쟁이나 논쟁이 갑자기 뜨거워질 때도 '불붙다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 신제품 출시로 두 회사의 경쟁이 불붙었어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불이 나는 것이 아니라 경쟁, 논쟁, 인기가 갑자기 뜨거워진다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not a real fire: a figure of speech for competition, debate or popularity suddenly getting intense.

explain_en: '불이 붙다' is the more common form; '불붙다' is written as one word. '불을 붙이다' is when someone sets something alight, while '불붙다' is it catching fire on its own. It is also used when a competition or debate suddenly heats up.

examples.en: A bee is buzzing by the window.
Mosquitoes buzzed all night, so I slept badly.
Cars went down the road with a humming roar.
A drone is buzzing overhead.
The humming sound of the fridge bothers me.
The child pushed a toy car, making vroom sounds.

explain: 벌, 모기, 기계, 엔진처럼 낮게 이어지는 소리를 흉내 내는 말이에요. '붕붕거리며', '붕붕거리는 소리'처럼 자주 써요. 아이들이 자동차 놀이를 하며 '붕붕' 소리를 내기도 해요. '붕붕대다'와 뜻이 같아요.
explain_en: It imitates a low, continuous sound made by bees, mosquitoes, machines or engines. It is often used as '붕붕거리며' or '붕붕거리는 소리'. Children also say '붕붕' while playing with toy cars. It means the same as '붕붕대다'.

en: circle; wheel around; make a turn

examples.en: The airplane is circling over the airport.
Birds slowly circle in the sky.

examples.ko: 헬리콥터가 산 위를 선회한 뒤 내려왔어요.
examples.en: The helicopter circled over the mountain and then came down.
The government suddenly turned its policy in another direction.
The sight of an eagle circling in the sky looks cool.

examples.ko: 배가 항구를 한 바퀴 선회할 때 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took a photo when the ship made a full circle around the port.

explain: 비행기, 새, 배가 큰 원을 그리며 돌거나, 비유로 정책과 입장을 크게 바꾼다는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '돌다'를 쓰고, 선회하다는 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요. 정책이나 태도가 바뀔 때는 '방향을 선회하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It describes aircraft, birds, or ships moving in a big circle, and figuratively a policy or position changing greatly. In daily talk people use '돌다', while 선회하다 appears more in news and writing. When policy or attitude changes, you say '방향을 선회하다'.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 거리를 쏘다니다가 저녁 늦게 친구를 찾아갔어요.
examples.en: After wandering the streets all day, I visited my friend late in the evening.

examples.ko: 방학인데 집에만 있지 않고 여기저기 쏘다녀요.
examples.en: It's vacation, so he doesn't stay home but roams around everywhere.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 어딜 그렇게 쏘다녔어요?
examples.en: Where did you run around like that on a rainy day?
Stop running around and do your homework at home first.
The kids are playing, running around the alley.

examples.ko: 서울을 쏘다니는 동안 길을 많이 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: While roaming around Seoul, I came to know a lot of streets.

explain: '돌아다니다'는 중립적이지만 '쏘다니다'는 이리저리 쉬지 않고 다니는 모습을 조금 못마땅하게 보는 느낌이 있어요. '싸다니다', '싸돌아다니다'와 비슷한 계열이에요. 자기 이야기를 가볍게 할 때는 괜찮지만 윗사람의 행동에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: '돌아다니다' is neutral, but '쏘다니다' carries a mildly disapproving feel about someone going back and forth without rest. It belongs to the same family as '싸다니다' and '싸돌아다니다'. It is fine when lightly talking about yourself, but don't use it for the actions of someone senior.

examples.en: The city hall built a park by the river.
The teacher created a comfortable atmosphere for us.

examples.ko: 친구들과 돈을 모아 기금을 조성할 거예요.
examples.en: We will pool our money and set up a fund.
The people who created the forest received an award.

examples.ko: 마을 정원을 조성하는 데 오 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took five years to create the village garden.

examples.ko: 학생들이 공부하기 좋은 환경을 조성하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to create a good environment for students to study.

explain: '만들다'는 아무 때나 쓰지만 '조성하다'는 공원·기금·분위기·환경처럼 큰 대상에 써요. 작은 물건이나 음식에는 쓰지 않아요. '분위기를 조성하다', '환경을 조성하다'가 가장 많이 쓰는 짝이에요.
explain_en: '만들다' works anywhere, but '조성하다' is for large targets such as parks, funds, atmospheres, and environments. It is not used for small objects or food. '분위기를 조성하다' and '환경을 조성하다' are the most common pairings.

en: watch closely; keep an eye on

examples.en: Everyone is closely watching the election results.
The police kept an eye on the suspect's movements.
Many people are watching exchange rate changes closely.
I will keep watching the situation from now on.
The teacher gazed steadily at me.
Experts watch the market and prepare a response.

explain: 눈으로 뚫어지게 본다는 느낌과 함께 '앞으로 어떻게 되는지 지켜본다'는 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스에서 '결과를 주시하다', '상황을 주시하다'로 아주 자주 나와요. 친구 사이에서는 '지켜보다'나 '쳐다보다'가 더 편해요.
explain_en: It combines staring intently with watching to see how things turn out. News uses 결과를 주시하다 and 상황을 주시하다 constantly. Among friends, 지켜보다 or 쳐다보다 feels more comfortable.

examples.en: The army began its advance at dawn.

examples.ko: 영화 속 진격 장면이 정말 웅장했어요.
examples.en: The charging scene in the movie was truly grand.
When the rain came, the enemy's advance slowed.

examples.ko: 우리 팀의 진격을 아무도 막지 못했어요.
examples.en: Nobody could stop our team's charge.
When the order to advance came, the soldiers stood up.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 장군의 진격 경로를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, I learned the general's route of advance.

explain: 진격은 군대가 적을 향해 앞으로 밀고 나아가는 일이에요. 스포츠에서 '우승을 향한 진격'처럼 기세 좋게 나아간다는 비유로도 써요. 반대로 뒤로 물러나는 일은 '후퇴'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means an army pushing forward toward the enemy. It is also used figuratively in sports, as in a team's drive toward the title. The opposite, moving backward, is 후퇴 (retreat).

examples.en: The gathering place is the school playground.
You must not be late for the assembly time.
Fire trucks assembled at the accident site.
Many people gathered in the square and cheered.

examples.ko: 집결 후에 버스를 타고 같이 이동해요.
examples.en: After assembling, we move together by bus.
Once the assembly was over, an announcement came on.

explain: 여러 사람이나 물건이 한곳으로 모이는 것을 말해요. '모임'이나 '모이다'보다 훨씬 딱딱하고 정해진 시간과 장소에 모일 때 써요. 단체 여행, 행사, 군대·소방 같은 곳에서 '집결 장소'라는 말을 자주 들어요.
explain_en: Many people or things gathering in one place. Much stiffer than '모임' or '모이다', and used for set times and places. You often hear '집결 장소' (assembly point) on group trips, events, and in the military or fire service.

examples.en: The airdrop of relief supplies has begun.
You need to decide the drop point precisely.

examples.ko: 물 투하는 바람이 약할 때 해야 해요.
examples.en: Water drops should be done when the wind is weak.

examples.ko: 비행기에서의 식량 투하로 마을 사람들이 살아났어요.
examples.en: The villagers survived thanks to the food dropped from a plane.

examples.ko: 산불 현장에서는 헬기의 소화약제 투하 작업이 한창이에요.
examples.en: At the wildfire site, helicopters are in the middle of dropping fire retardant.
The pilots trained for accurate drops.

explain: 비행기나 헬기에서 무언가를 아래로 떨어뜨리는 일을 말할 때 써요. 보통 '구호 물자 투하'처럼 앞에 물건 이름을 붙여요. 손으로 떨어뜨리는 일에는 쓰지 않고 '떨어뜨리다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used for dropping something down from an airplane or helicopter. The name of the item usually goes in front, as in 구호 물자 투하. It is not used for dropping something by hand; for that people say 떨어뜨리다.

en: form an array; take up a position

examples.ko: 대회 우승 후보들이 한 조에 포진해 있어요.
examples.en: The title contenders are all lined up in one group.

examples.ko: 이 팀은 중앙에 실력 좋은 선수들이 포진하고 있어요.
examples.en: This team has skilled players positioned in the center.

examples.ko: 역 앞에는 카페와 식당이 줄줄이 포진했어요.
examples.en: Cafés and restaurants have set up in a row in front of the station.

examples.ko: 인기 배우들이 이번 드라마에 대거 포진했어요.
examples.en: Many popular actors are in the cast of this drama.

examples.ko: 큰 서점들이 이 거리에 포진한 덕분에 책 구경하기 좋아요.
examples.en: Thanks to the big bookstores lined up on this street, it is great for browsing books.

examples.ko: 유명한 맛집이 시장 입구에 포진하면 손님이 몰려요.
examples.en: When famous restaurants cluster at the market entrance, customers flock there.

explain: '모여 있다'보다 어떤 자리에 짜임새 있게 자리 잡고 있다는 느낌이 있어요. 'A가 B에 포진해 있다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 쓰고, 스포츠나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Compared with '모여 있다' (be gathered), it feels like they have taken well-organized positions. It is used as 'A가 B에 포진해 있다' with the particle '에', and often appears in sports and news.

examples.en: The soldiers marched along the snowy road.
How many kilometers do you march per day?

examples.ko: 우리는 비가 오는데도 계속 행군해야 했어요.
examples.en: We had to keep marching even though it was raining.
The unit decided to march to the top of the mountain.
The soldiers are marching in line.
Everyone is exhausted from marching all night.

explain: 주로 군대가 훈련이나 이동을 위해 오래 걸을 때 써요. 퍼레이드나 시위처럼 줄지어 걷는 건 '행진하다'를 쓰는 게 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is mainly used when an army walks a long way for training or movement. For parades or protests, '행진하다' is the more natural verb.

examples.en: The students march around the field in line.
The soldiers marched in the wide square.
People sang while marching down the street.

examples.ko: 축제 퍼레이드가 시청 앞까지 행진할 거예요.
examples.en: The festival parade will march up to the city hall.
Children gathered to see the marching band.

examples.ko: 우리는 다 같이 행진하고 나서 점심을 먹었어요.
examples.en: After marching together, we had lunch.

explain: 여럿이 줄을 맞춰 걸을 때 써요. 그냥 걷는 '걷다'와 달리 박자나 목적이 있는 느낌이에요. 축제 퍼레이드, 군대, 운동회에서 자주 나와요. 혼자 걷는 일에는 거의 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Use it when many people walk together in line. Unlike plain '걷다', it feels rhythmic or purposeful. It comes up at festival parades, in the military and at sports days, and is almost never used for one person walking alone.

examples.en: The child heard the sound and jumped up.

examples.ko: 늦잠을 자서 후다닥 옷을 입고 나왔어요.
examples.en: I overslept, so I threw on my clothes and rushed out.

examples.ko: 선생님이 오시자 학생들이 후다닥 자리에 앉았어요.
examples.en: When the teacher came, the students scrambled into their seats.
The cat dashed under the bed.
I finished the dishes in a flash and watched a drama.

examples.ko: 비가 오기 시작하자 사람들이 후다닥 뛰어갔어요.
examples.en: When it started to rain, people dashed off.

explain: 급하게 재빨리 움직이는 모습을 흉내 낸 말이라 일어나다, 뛰다, 숨다, 끝내다 같은 동작과 잘 어울려요. 후닥닥과 쓰임이 거의 같아요. 보통 '후다닥 ~하다'처럼 동사 앞에 놓아요.
explain_en: It imitates the look of moving in a hurry, so it goes well with actions like getting up, running, hiding and finishing. It is used almost the same as 후닥닥. It normally sits right before a verb, as in '후다닥 ~하다'.
